analysis.one_liner: Tata Consumer Products sells packaged tea, coffee and salt (Tata Tea, Tetley, Tata Salt) plus a growing foods basket - Sampann, Ching's Secret, Soulfull, Organic India - in India and abroad, and holds a 50:50 stake in Tata Starbucks cafes.
analysis.whats_happening: In the June 2026 quarter (Q1 FY27), revenue grew about 12% to roughly Rs 5,349 crore, EBITDA rose 19% to Rs 730 crore (margin up 70 basis points to 13.6%), and profit grew 28% to about Rs 427 crore, led by newer categories - Sampann, ready-to-drink beverages, Capital Foods, Organic India and Soulfull - which grew 47% year-on-year. The company also raised its stake in Capital Foods (maker of Ching's Secret) to 80% around September 2026, continuing a phased buyout that began in January 2024. The September 2026 quarter's results have not been announced yet as of this writing; going by last year's timing they are likely due in early-to-mid November, but no confirmed date was found.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a household-name FMCG company - think Tata Tea, Tata Salt, Tetley, and newer bets like Ching's noodles masala and Soulfull millet snacks. The core tea and salt business grows steadily in low double digits, but the real growth story right now is the newer, smaller categories growing near 50% a year and slowly becoming a bigger share of the business. The tension: the stock trades at a rich price relative to how much profit the company actually earns on its capital (return on equity is a modest 7-8%), so you're paying up for the hope that these newer, faster-growing pieces keep expanding and lift margins - not for current cash returns.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026): revenue ~Rs 5,349 crore (+11.9% YoY), EBITDA ~Rs 730 crore (+19% YoY, margin +70bps to 13.6%), consolidated PAT ~Rs 427 crore (+28% YoY). Management flagged tea input cost inflation of 7-10% and said price hikes were taken in June 2026, with margin guidance of 50-70bps expansion maintained for FY27. No explicit 'not comparable' flag was found for this specific quarter, though the GST rate rationalisation of September 2025 (tea cut to 5%, salt to 0%, namkeens to 5%) continues to affect the base against which growth is measured - worth keeping in mind when reading percentage changes. Full FY26: revenue crossed Rs 20,000 crore (+15%), PAT Rs 1,547 crore (+20%).
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 22.3% from its May 2026 peak of Rs 1,260 to the current Rs 978.9. This is a genuine market derating, not a corporate-action distortion - the only split on record is a 10:1 split from June 2010, long since reflected in the price history, and there has been no recent demerger or spin-off that would understate returns. Against that, over 3 and 5 years the stock has clearly beaten its FMCG peer HUL, which has actually lost money for shareholders over both periods (down ~22% over 3Y and 5Y), but TATACONSUM has lagged the Nifty (10.3% vs 16.8% over 3Y; 20.9% vs 25.3% over 5Y). Over the last year both stock and sector were weak, with the stock falling less (-14.1%) than its peer (-24.7%) but more than the Nifty (-9.5%).
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 58-59x and P/B of 4.45x, this is an expensive stock on any conventional measure, and notably expensive against a return on equity of just 7.35% and ROCE of 9.24%. Why it is priced this way: the market is paying for Tata Group brand trust, pricing power in staples, and optionality on the newer growth categories (Capital Foods, Sampann, RTD, Soulfull) which are compounding near 50% a year and lifting margins. Whether it is actually cheap: no - on current profitability the multiple only makes sense if that growth-business momentum and margin expansion continue for several more years; a stumble there would leave the valuation looking stretched relative to the underlying returns the business generates today.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is volume-led at the core - management cited 13% underlying volume growth in the India branded business - with an increasingly important margin-accretive layer coming from newer categories (Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods, Organic India, Soulfull) that grew 47% YoY and now make up 36% of the India business, up from 28% a year earlier. So this isn't pricing-driven growth theatre; both volumes and a richer mix are contributing, and EBITDA margin has actually expanded (+70bps in the latest quarter) rather than being flat or eroding.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk looks low: debt-to-equity is around 0.12 and the company sits in a net cash position, so leverage is not the concern. The more relevant risk is business risk - input cost inflation in tea (7-10%) squeezing margins unless price hikes stick, competitive intensity in packaged foods, and the fact that return on equity (7.35%) is still modest for a company commanding a near-59x earnings multiple, meaning profits are not yet translating into the kind of capital efficiency the valuation implies.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters - Tata Sons (28.68%) and Tata Investment Corporation (4.65%) - together hold 33.83%, with no pledging disclosed, which is reassuring from a governance standpoint. Institutional ownership is substantial: FIIs hold about 20.08% and domestic institutions 24.99%, with Nippon India Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund the largest named mutual fund holders. No evidence was found of any well-known individual 'star' investor holding a disclosed stake - worth noting plainly rather than assuming one exists.
strengths: Q1 FY27 profit grew 28% YoY to about Rs 427 crore on 12% revenue growth, with EBITDA margin expanding 70bps to 13.6%
Net cash balance sheet with debt-to-equity of only about 0.12 - low financial risk
Newer growth categories (Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods, Organic India, Soulfull) grew 47% YoY and now account for 36% of the India business, up from 28%
Stable promoter holding of 33.83% (Tata Sons plus Tata Investment Corp) with no pledging
watchpoints: Return on equity of just 7.35% sits awkwardly against a near-59x P/E - the valuation assumes a lot more capital efficiency than the business currently delivers
Tea input costs rising 7-10%; June 2026 price hikes were taken but pass-through to volumes is unproven
Stock is down 22.3% from its May 2026 peak and has underperformed the Nifty over both 3 and 5 years
Tata Starbucks (50:50 JV) remained loss-making in FY26 (Rs 49 crore loss) in its 14th year of operation, even as the loss narrowed from Rs 136 crore
analysis.one_thing: Whether the newer 'growth businesses' (Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods, Organic India, Soulfull) keep compounding near 40-50% and continue lifting consolidated EBITDA margin - that trajectory is what would justify today's roughly 59x earnings multiple against a sub-8% return on equity.
analysis.data_notes: P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, debt and shareholding figures cross-checked primarily against Screener.in, which was internally consistent; other aggregators gave shareholding splits that didn't sum to 100% and were discarded. Q1 FY27 results cross-checked across Business Standard, Investing.com and a GuruFocus earnings-call summary. The quoted 10-year profit CAGR of 68% looks skewed by a low base year and should not be read as a steady-state growth rate - the 5-year figure (12%) is more representative. Q2 FY27 results date and FY24 segment-level EBITDA/PAT figures could not be independently confirmed - treat as 'not verified - check on Screener' where cited.
